summary.headline: FY26 was a down year: management guides ~18% FY27 volume growth while declining to disclose EBITDA quantum; Q4 realisations fell on lower-cost 2025 crop inventory.
summary.overview: Foods & Inns reported a challenging FY26 with lower realisations from pass-through of lower raw material costs, export disruption from the March geopolitical situation, and lower tomato processing volumes from poor crop quality. Management said FY26 volume grew about 4% overall (domestic about 3%, exports about 6%), against an earlier expectation of 10%. Management guides about 18% volume growth for FY27, led by frozen foods and Tetra Recart, but gave no absolute EBITDA guidance because the model is cost-plus. Management also highlighted solar additions, the FY25 PLI receipt of INR33.86 crores, and commissioning of pectin and spray-drying capacity.

financial_highlights.value: about 25% YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

financial_highlights.change: down INR16 crores from INR427 crores; about INR10 crores more at Kusum

financial_highlights.metric: FY25 PLI incentive received and recognised

financial_highlights.value: about INR83 crores of total INR145 crores
about INR29 crores (vs about INR160 crores last year)
financial_highlights.change: management says combined position is similar year on year

segments.name: Pulping / mango processing
segments.commentary: Production runs mid-April to early August and contributes more than 75% of volume; about 45-50% of stock carries forward into the next year. Export dispatch is spread evenly, while domestic dispatch is concentrated December to June.

segments.name: Frozen foods
segments.commentary: Volume grew about 28% in FY26; management expects this to be the main FY27 growth driver. Frozen gross margin is about 50%, but cold-chain costs sit below gross margin.

segments.name: Spray drying / Tetra Recart
segments.commentary: Spray-drying capacity expansion of 120 MTPA targets commercial run in December. Tetra Recart has confirmed orders of about 400 MT (about INR8 crores); management targets about INR20 crores of business in FY27. Capex was about INR30 crores (INR24 crores machinery, INR6 crores building).

segments.name: Pectin
segments.commentary: Commercial production started about 7-8 days before the call after teething issues. Management expects about 50% capacity use this year, implying INR7-8 crores revenue and gross margin of about 70%. Capacity is 150 MT against India imports of about 350 MT.

segments.name: Kusum Spices
segments.commentary: Sales were hit in March by the war. Oman and the Gulf are major destinations; diversification to Europe and Southeast Asia is at a preliminary stage.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 18% for the total basket (confirmed as overall portfolio, not just mango and tomato); one answer cited 17%.
No absolute EBITDA or margin-percentage guidance; management says the model is a cost-plus pass-through and margin will rise with mix.
Spray-drying 120 MTPA expansion expected to start commercial run in December, with 2.5-3 months of benefit in FY27.
Tetra Recart FY27 business target about INR20 crores; total capacity value about INR80 crores plus.
Frozen ambition: segment at about INR100 crores to grow to INR300-400 crores in 3-4 years, subject to an NHB cluster programme with approval in principle and details expected in about a month.
Debt: long-term debt about INR71-72 crores with about INR20 crores annual repayment, to be met from internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Spray-drying line expansion of 120 MTPA; commercial run targeted December.
Pectin plant (150 MT capacity) commissioned; wet peel now processed alongside dry peel.
Solar: about 1,300 kWp each at Vankal and Gonde, added in May 2026, not capitalised at 31 March; payback below 3 years.
Tetra Recart building has room for 3 more machines.
Management expects little further capex after the NHB cluster project; cluster capex details pending.
demand_pricing: Q4 volumes hit by the March Middle East situation; Europe and US dispatches were delayed about 15 days by vessel unavailability, and goods shipped in April-May.
GCC exposure is small at about USD2-3 million; a gas shortage at the spray-drying facility cut production for about 45 days from mid-March to April, now normalised at higher cost.
Domestic Q4 volume was down YoY on a high base from the UP Kumbh Mela campaign last year; beverage brands are growing about 8-9%.
Raw-material prices expected similar to or lower than last year; low-realisation inventory from the 2025 crop will carry into FY27 and FY28.
Tomato stock of about 9,000 MT is fully back-to-back ordered; expected to clear in about 45 days, worth about INR70-75 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise when procurement was low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said borrowings fell by about INR16 crores to INR411 crores standalone (INR427 crores last year); Kusum adds about INR10 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Was inventory up 30% as the balance sheet suggests?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory plus vendor advances fell to about INR29 crores from about INR160 crores last year, so total working capital tied up is similar; table-variety fruit was cheap to procure after Alphonso exports were disrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback or promoter buying planned with the stock below book value?
qa_highlights.answer: The promoter said he has made some inter-promoter purchases and expects more disclosures; the CFO said debt reduction comes first and a buyback is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of El Nino on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say. Mango is over 75% of turnover and management sees little sourcing risk; vegetable sourcing may be affected, and price volatility is the main risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pectin ramp-up and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production started recently; about 50% utilisation expected this year, yielding INR7-8 crores revenue at about 70% gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to reach the INR300-400 crore frozen target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the frozen segment is about INR100 crores today; details on the NHB cluster programme and capex are expected in about a month.

risks_watch: Volume delivery against the 18% FY27 target; FY26 volume was about 4% against an earlier 10% expectation.
Realisations: low-cost 2025 crop inventory will be sold through FY27 and possibly FY28.
El Nino and crop quality risk for mango and vegetables; the tomato crop failed last year.
Export disruption from West Asia and vessel availability for US and Europe; Kusum Spices depends on Gulf and Oman.
Tetra Recart offtake remains slow; large brands have not yet signed, and the Indian retort market is not established.
Gas supply reliability for the spray-drying facility.
Working capital intensity and stock-holding for MNC customers; debt reduction depends on internal accruals.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and volume targets, but evasive on EBITDA and margin quantum, citing the pass-through model. Management was candid about FY26 setbacks (crop, war, gas) and defensive on the share price and buyback question.
key_quotes: Considering the present situation and market scenario or information, whatever update we are getting from customers, we are expecting around 18% volume growth for this financial year.
As always, our pricing remains a direct pass-through of raw material movements.
So INR7 - 8 crores of revenue is what we can actually expect at 50% utilization and the gross margins are approximately around 70%-odd of that.
So buyback might be the last thing on our mind.

adds.what: Pectin plant 150 MT capacity (commissioned, commercial production started about 7-8 days before call)
Tetra Recart machine capacity (building has room for 3 more machines)

growth.why: Management guides ~18% FY27 volume growth across the portfolio, led by frozen foods (FY26 up ~28%) and Tetra Recart (~INR20 crore target, ~400 MT confirmed orders), with pectin at 50% utilisation of 150 MT and a 120 MTPA spray-drying expansion from December; no EBITDA guidance given, and Q4 realisation fell ~25% YoY on pass-through pricing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: No EBITDA or margin % guidance; management says the cost-plus model passes through costs and margin rises with mix (frozen gross margin ~50%, pectin ~70%), but Q4 realisations fell ~25% YoY and low-cost 2025 crop inventory carries into FY27-FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (spray-drying commercial run targeted December 2026)
rows.why: 120 MTPA spray-drying line expansion (INR30 crore capex, INR24 crore machinery) is under construction with commercial run targeted December; pectin 150 MT is already commissioned and solar of ~1,300 kWp each at Vankal and Gonde was added May 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides ~18% FY27 volume growth across the portfolio, led by frozen (FY26 up ~28%) and Tetra Recart (~400 MT confirmed orders, ~INR20 crore FY27 target), against only ~4% FY26 growth versus an earlier 10% expectation, so delivery risk is real.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: next 1-2 months for NHB cluster details; little further cape
rows.why: Frozen ambition of INR300-400 crore in 3-4 years is subject to an NHB cluster programme with approval in principle, details expected in about a month; management expects little capex after that, and utilisation is not disclosed ("not 100% utilised").

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 volume was ~4% against an earlier ~10% expectation, Q4 realisations fell ~25% YoY, and management gave no absolute EBITDA guidance, so there is no sign of an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 volume missed its ~10% expectation (came in ~4%), the 18% FY27 target depends on Tetra Recart offtake that remains slow with large brands unsigned, and El Nino and export/vessel disruption are open risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tetra Recart commercial scale-up (~400 MT confirmed orders, ~INR20 crore FY27 target, building has room for 3 more machines) and pectin ramp (50% of 150 MT, INR7-8 crore revenue at ~70% gross margin) are already under way.

rows.label: Tomato stock fully back-to-back ordered
rows.why: About 9,000 MT of tomato stock is fully back-to-back ordered and expected to clear in about 45 days, worth INR70-75 crore.

rows.label: Borrowings down INR16 crore to INR411 crore
rows.why: Standalone borrowings fell from INR427 crore to INR411 crore, long-term debt is ~INR71-72 crore with ~INR20 crore annual repayment from internal accruals, and the CFO put debt reduction ahead of any buyback.

rows.label: Gas supply reliability at spray-drying facility
rows.why: A gas shortage cut spray-drying production for about 45 days from mid-March to April at higher cost, and reliability is a stated risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 18% FY27 volume target, frozen growth and Tetra Recart, but evasive on EBITDA and margin quantum (citing cost-plus pass-through) and defensive on buyback and share price; analysts pressed on borrowings, inventory build, realisation decline and FY26 volume miss.
